title: Segmentation & Scoring Framework for Enterprise Security Requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Establish a deterministic segmentation and numeric scoring system for incoming enterprise security & compliance requests (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires). Purpose: enable consistent prioritization, automated routing to owners (Legal, Security, Compliance, Solutions), and SLA-backed response windows that align with commercial motions (self-serve, sales-assisted, enterprise).
acceptance_criteria: A documented scoring rubric that maps inputs to a single priority score (0-100) and a routing destination
Automation rules implemented in intake form to attach initial score and route to the right owner
SLA table agreed with Legal/Security for High/Medium/Low segments and published in the intake UX
Two pilot customers (sales-assisted) triaged using the framework with post-triage feedback collected
Instrumentation: every intake has score, assigned owner, triage timestamp, and resolution_timestamp logged
triage_flow: 1) Intake submission via Security Request form / Partner Portal / Sales ticket
2) Automated enrichment: customer tier, contract tags (HIPAA/GDPR), region, and model/data sensitivity flags pulled from CRM and contracts DB
3) Scoring engine computes priority score using rubric below
4) If score >= 75 => route to Security + Legal (High) and create urgent Slack alert to #sec-urgent
5) If score 50-74 => route to Security (Medium) and to Solutions Eng for technical intake
6) If score < 50 => route to Compliance backlog with suggested response template
7) Owner acknowledges within SLA, records mitigation plan, and updates intake ticket
8) Post-resolution: QA review and update scoring thresholds if needed (quarterly)
scoring_rubric: Regulatory Domain (weight 30): HIPAA/Finance=30, GDPR/DPA=20, SOC2/ISO=15, Non-regulatory vendor questionnaires=10
Data Sensitivity (weight 20): PHI/PII critical=20, PII limited=12, Non-sensitive=5
Contractual SLA Exposure (weight 10): Obligation already in contract and penalty=10, No contractual obligation=0
Operational Complexity (weight 10): Requires infra changes/on-prem deploy=10, Documentation/process only=3
Time-to-resolution constraint (weight 5): Customer requires <7 days=5, 7-30 days=3, >30 days=0
Example: Enterprise HIPAA request with PHI + contractual penalty => 25+30+20+10+10+5 = 100
routing_rules: Score >= 85: High — Immediate Security + Legal involvement, exec escalation to AE/CS, target TTR 5 business days
Score 65-84: Medium — Security + Solutions Eng review, target TTR 15 business days
Score 40-64: Low — Compliance/PM review, standard response templates, target TTR 30 business days
Score <40: Info — Automated response with docs, owner = Compliance docs team, target TTR 60 days
Special-case override: Any request flagged as regulator notice or government inquiry -> route to Legal Ops immediately regardless of score
SLAs: High: acknowledge in 4 business hours, initial mitigation proposal in 48 hours, resolution target 5 business days
Medium: acknowledge in 1 business day, proposal in 7 business days, resolution target 15 business days
Low: acknowledge in 3 business days, proposal in 14 business days, resolution target 30 business days
Escalation path: If owner misses acknowledge SLA, automated escalations to Security Manager and Head of Product after SLA breach
automation_tasks: Add scoring engine to intake Lambda; expose score as ticket field in Linear
CRM integration: fetch contract tags (HIPAA/GDPR) and customer tier at submit time
Slack routing: automated alerts for High/critical scores into #sec-urgent and customer AE channels
Populate recommended response template based on score and regulatory domain
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: Finalize rubric with Legal & Security; build mockups of intake UX showing score and SLA
Week 3-4: Implement scoring engine and CRM enrichment; unit test with synthetic cases
Week 5: Run 2-week pilot with Sales (two enterprise customers) and Compliance; collect feedback
Week 6: Iterate thresholds, add automation, and prepare docs/training for Solutions/Legal
Week 7: GA rollout; monitor metrics and hold weekly review for first 4 weeks

decisions: Use a single numeric score (0-100) instead of multi-dimensional buckets to simplify routing and metrics
Weight regulatory domain and customer tier highest to reflect commercial and legal risk
Automate initial routing but allow human override by Security or Legal
Pilot must include two active sales-assisted customers to validate real-world edge-cases
